<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9423e2b362f37cef">Does retaining expert parameters mean P²-MOPD runs multiple experts at inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ap2-mopd">P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Australian Institute for Machine Learning, Adelaide University / StepFun</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Task vectors are training-time optimization directions; the forward pass uses one materialized student weight tensor. Coefficient increments fold into ordinary weights, and exported inference needs neither teachers nor coefficient metadata. Teacher scoring and parameter priors are two training roles, not inference-time ensemble voting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: W=B+0.3τ1+0.2τ2 is composed into one matrix and inputs multiply W, rather than voting across three outputs. Local code updates matrices without loading expert models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03953v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.03953-p2-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9423e2b362f37cef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:p2-mopd" data-paper-title="P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a971b984d3dad311">Why compute P²-MOPD coefficient gradients before clipping student gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ap2-mopd">P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Australian Institute for Machine Learning, Adelaide University / StepFun</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The paper sends the same pre-update gradient through two independently budgeted channels. Coefficient gradients are inner products of unclipped G and fixed task vectors; weight and coefficient channels are then globally clipped separately. Clipping G first lets the weight budget prematurely scale the coefficient channel, changing relative updates and Adam state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: G=[3,4] and τ=[2,0] give coefficient gradient 6. Clipping G to norm 0.01 first gives an inner product of 0.012, no longer the prescribed raw coefficient gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03953v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.03953-p2-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a971b984d3dad311">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:p2-mopd" data-paper-title="P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3366298f665c46d">How does P²-MOPD differ from learning only task-arithmetic coefficients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ap2-mopd">P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Australian Institute for Machine Learning, Adelaide University / StepFun</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coefficient-only merging stays in the fixed task vectors&#x27; affine span. P²-MOPD retains full free student weights, preserving the model class of an ordinary student and allowing motion outside that span. It changes optimization geometry and reachability along expert directions, not inference parameter capacity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: With only task direction [1,0], coefficient updates cannot change coordinate two, but free student weights can move along [0,1]. Small-tensor checks establish this freedom, not actual recovery across four domains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03953v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.03953-p2-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3366298f665c46d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:p2-mopd" data-paper-title="P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-26cfaf0d6779523e">What breaks multi-step equivalence between materialized W and explicit B plus coefficients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ap2-mopd">P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Australian Institute for Machine Learning, Adelaide University / StepFun</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nonzero weight decay shrinks W and B differently, adding unintended task-vector shrinkage. Both channels also need independent optimizer state and the same pre-update gradient. Non-finite gradients or norms must skip the entire step rather than updating one channel before discovering the other&#x27;s failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: With B=1, ατ=1 and W=2, identical decay settings shrink W twice as much as B. Updating W before stopping on a NaN coefficient gradient likewise leaves a partial step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果、负控与边界, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03953v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.03953-p2-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26cfaf0d6779523e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:targeted-guidance" data-paper-title="Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-targeted-guidance-8f74e1a3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac8c3bab0fb173c1">Does Targeted Guidance need a larger external teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atargeted-guidance">Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Cursor Research / UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Its teacher shares student weights but receives textual feedback immediately before a failed turn, with teacher gradients stopped. Feedback must first be independently checked to improve the intended criterion. Identical parameters need not imply identical conditional distributions; the local loss interface does not fabricate feedback effectiveness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: After a student omits a tool argument, the feedback-conditioned branch sees a reminder to provide the returned-line count. It can score the same prefix differently, but this does not let a deployed student see future errors or gold answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05266v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.05266-targeted-guidance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac8c3bab0fb173c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:targeted-guidance" data-paper-title="Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bec61c4d24dd2dfc">Why does the KL denominator include all response tokens when only one turn fails?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atargeted-guidance">Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Cursor Research / UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gating selects where auxiliary distillation gradients apply; whole-response normalization controls the rollout&#x27;s total pressure. Dividing only by failed tokens amplifies a tiny error to full average distillation strength. Nonfailed turns have zero auxiliary gradient but their valid response tokens still count in the denominator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: If one failed token among 100 response tokens has KL 2, the contribution is 2/100. Dividing by failed-token count gives 2, a 100-fold amplification. Padding must not count among those 100 tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05266v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.05266-targeted-guidance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bec61c4d24dd2dfc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:targeted-guidance" data-paper-title="Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3a392e71e57d0bc">Why not replace failed-turn reverse KL plus RL with whole-trajectory OPSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atargeted-guidance">Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Cursor Research / UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The method restricts its auxiliary signal to failures, uses full-vocabulary student-to-frozen-teacher KL and retains ordinary per-criterion RL rewards. Whole-trajectory distillation keeps pressuring already compliant behavior, changing diversity and the primary task. Forward KL and sampled-token estimators are also different numerical objectives. The auxiliary term disappears once every criterion passes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: If one tool turn is valid and the next invalid, only the latter receives auxiliary gradients. Once both are valid, recover the original GRPO objective instead of continuing to imitate every aspect of the feedback teacher&#x27;s style.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 论文离线与线上效果, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05266v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.05266-targeted-guidance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3a392e71e57d0bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:targeted-guidance" data-paper-title="Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3a228c8c816cff2">Do failed-turn masks and the loss complete the paper&#x27;s coding-agent training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atargeted-guidance">Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Cursor Research / UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The caller still owns actual student sampling, criterion judgments, feedback placement and screening, same-prefix teacher scoring, external GRPO advantages and the tool environment. The component checks masks and gradients. Giving an evaluated agent gold answers or fixed correct actions breaks evaluation; a success rate of one would not repair that boundary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Checking zero nonfailed-token gradients with small random logits is a valid L1 test. Placing hidden test answers in student history to correct it and then claiming a coding pass-rate improvement is leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与代码映射, 结果、负控与边界, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05266v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.05266-targeted-guidance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3a228c8c816cff2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:aopd" data-paper-title="When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-aopd-187dc1ba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d373390c70e780e">Why ask whether the student can complete an AOPD teacher action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aaopd">When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher&#x27;s favored next step may be beyond student continuation skill. Relative terminal advantage measures usable guidance from existing student rollouts without counterfactual generations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An advanced proof start is not useful if the student cannot continue it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31563v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.31563-aopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d373390c70e780e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:aopd" data-paper-title="When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7838986bdda19e05">Why do both AOPD terms share a truncated teacher measure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aaopd">When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The estimator combines terms that cancel to measure teacher-action advantage for student continuation. Clipping only one or renormalizing changes the objective. Use other same-prompt rollouts for LOO, with frozen teacher/behavior and no new counterfactual continuations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Evaluate a teacher-preferred opening against the student&#x27;s actual returns rather than reinforce it solely from teacher likelihood.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31563v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.31563-aopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7838986bdda19e05">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:aopd" data-paper-title="When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-11c650f807871930">How does AOPD differ from multiplying KL by reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aaopd">When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It includes a sampled term and full-distribution term under the same unnormalized truncated teacher measure, plus independent leave-one-out returns. Simple reward multiplication loses that estimator structure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weighting one sampled word doesn&#x27;t reproduce subtraction of the vocabulary-wide term.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31563v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.31563-aopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-11c650f807871930">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:aopd" data-paper-title="When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fc0623d19d76044">Can AOPD clip only the sampled term or replace rollout S with current student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aaopd">When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Both terms share the unnormalized truncated teacher measure; denominator is frozen rollout S. Update only Sθ, with groups larger than one for independent LOO. Don&#x27;t change behavior probabilities across steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Re-softmax after truncation changes total mass and correspondence between terms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31563v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.31563-aopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fc0623d19d76044">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minimal-edit-opd" data-paper-title="Edit, Don&#x27;t Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-minimal-edit-opd-97f1b5ed" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-622a1fc443b1a5c7">Why skip teacher correction for correct ME-OPD replies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminimal-edit-opd">Edit, Don&#x27;t Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Successful traces retain task reward without stylistic interference. Failures alone select original tokens the teacher supports less. The teacher scores existing responses instead of writing new ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not rewrite a valid alternative solution just because its style differs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30231v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30231-minimal-edit-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-622a1fc443b1a5c7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minimal-edit-opd" data-paper-title="Edit, Don&#x27;t Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c91dbc6c4760e464">Why skip correction for successes and select only some tokens from failures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminimal-edit-opd">Edit, Don&#x27;t Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Preserve successful student behavior with task reward. Compare teacher and old student only for errors, correcting less teacher-supported tokens. Full group advantage precedes split. Reference solution and full reply are teacher training inputs only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A misread geometry label can receive focused suppression without reworking a successful alternative response.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30231v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30231-minimal-edit-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c91dbc6c4760e464">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minimal-edit-opd" data-paper-title="Edit, Don&#x27;t Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1965d1730d240a81">How do ME-OPD and Projected Distillation produce corrections differently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminimal-edit-opd">Edit, Don&#x27;t Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ME-OPD teacher-forces and suppresses chosen original error tokens. Projected Distillation generates a verified revision and compares edited spans via DPO. Scoring existing tokens and producing paired text differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Only the latter needs a newly written answer aligned to the original.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30231v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30231-minimal-edit-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1965d1730d240a81">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minimal-edit-opd" data-paper-title="Edit, Don&#x27;t Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-66ee5b0fc573399b">Compute ME-OPD group advantages before or after splitting successes and failures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminimal-edit-opd">Edit, Don&#x27;t Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use all K rewards before splitting. A success-only group has constant reward. Use frozen old student for strict-greater mask and divide by selected correction tokens across the minibatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher and old student ties are not selected; do not remake mask from updated scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30231v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.30231-minimal-edit-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66ee5b0fc573399b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:csd" data-paper-title="CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-csd-2e95adef" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b6013f196c2b334">Why align shared textual events rather than token IDs in CSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acsd">CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tokenizers differ in IDs, vocabulary and segmentation. Verify decoded character spans, then compare probability of common text events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One tokenizer can split a word in two; identical IDs wouldn&#x27;t establish matching text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28895v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b6013f196c2b334">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:csd" data-paper-title="CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1963fb419fddeb23">Why preserve REST across tokenizers rather than softmax common matches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acsd">CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Build common text events from verified decoded boundaries and chain probabilities. REST carries omitted mass; renormalization discards it and changes divergence. Don&#x27;t align by position or IDs alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two tokens and one token may express one word, but unmatched continuation probability still exists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28895v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1963fb419fddeb23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:csd" data-paper-title="CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-efd7158acfdbd08a">What does REST preserve that renormalizing common candidates removes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acsd">CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It retains probability of unmatched events instead of pretending their intersection is the whole distribution. Do not replace chain probability with a length mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A small shared intersection may appear very similar after softmax while most mass was omitted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28895v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efd7158acfdbd08a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:csd" data-paper-title="CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-59295ed90b381ba1">Do CSD student gradients flow only through the final token of a chunk?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acsd">CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Include prefix chain factors, final token and REST. Freeze teacher. Non-1:1 weights don&#x27;t enter denominator count; fall back to CE for no KD/shared event and detach overall ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ignoring the first of two pieces miscomputes its entire text event.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28895v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-59295ed90b381ba1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:visually-attributable-opd" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-visually-attributable-opd-08abcb9d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c05fa0a31b262be">Why compare evidence-preserving and degraded crops in VAG?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avisually-attributable-opd">Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Privileged corrections can mix visual evidence with style. Contrast matched visual conditions to estimate direction, retain agreeing corrections and bound modulation of verifier advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After cropping, check whether a teacher&#x27;s revision follows changed visual evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26856v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.26856-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6c05fa0a31b262be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:visually-attributable-opd" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9db3e7df89d58559">Why accept only teacher corrections matching the visual contrast sign?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avisually-attributable-opd">Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Privileged crop changes may be stylistic. Require compatible evidence direction and use bounded modulation of verifier advantage. Only visual input changes in same EMA model; arbitrary text logits and local documentation do not reproduce the chain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If preference changes after privileged crop but not after occluding evidence, don&#x27;t automatically treat it as visual guidance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26856v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.26856-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9db3e7df89d58559">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:visually-attributable-opd" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0a9fabe889a4cbd9">How does VAG differ from fixed textual teacher logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avisually-attributable-opd">Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The definition needs the same EMA vision model under real paired views. Fixed logits only simulate the formula, not visual sensitivity or attribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two manually supplied scores aren&#x27;t an occlusion experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26856v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.26856-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0a9fabe889a4cbd9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:visually-attributable-opd" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3aece6b9cdc6db6">Can VAG&#x27;s teacher branches be different models, and was this run?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avisually-attributable-opd">Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not under the same protocol: one EMA teacher, only visual input changes. The local page describes equations without executing multimodal training. Keep strict sign agreement and verifier advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Comparing a large vision teacher to a small text model confounds architecture and evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26856v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.26856-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3aece6b9cdc6db6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:apsd" data-paper-title="Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-apsd-7a5d9aba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b2643095f7c4d5ec">Why interpolate APSD successes but extrapolate beyond teacher for failures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aapsd">Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success should retain existing student preferences with gentle interpolation. Failures use stronger teacher-direction correction. Feedback selects a target regime, not guaranteed correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use lighter changes after a correct response and stronger correction after failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.25973-apsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2643095f7c4d5ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:apsd" data-paper-title="Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-975d7ed4ab0090e0">Why freeze only APSD teacher rather than detach the interpolated/extrapolated target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aapsd">Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Target depends on current student as well as teacher. Detach loses the student coupling that differs for success/failure. Forward equality doesn&#x27;t imply backward equality. Feedback is privileged training context only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical target probabilities can yield different parameter updates when only one graph retains target dependence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.25973-apsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-975d7ed4ab0090e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:apsd" data-paper-title="Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5fd715ce12c8bbea">Why isn&#x27;t freezing APSD self-teacher the same as detaching its entire target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aapsd">Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher q is frozen, but product-of-experts target also depends differentiably on p. Whole-target detach removes a defining coupling term, despite identical forward values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Detaching a target branch partly built from current student changes optimization, not merely memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.25973-apsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5fd715ce12c8bbea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:apsd" data-paper-title="Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0cdab3eae9b2f49">Which PoE tensors retain APSD gradients, and how interpret default α?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aapsd">Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student and its target branch are differentiable, teacher detached. Use log space to avoid underflow. Correct α is between zero and one, error α above one. Local RLRF settings differ from paper RLVR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Local 0.5 and 1.5 aren&#x27;t universal paper settings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.25973-apsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0cdab3eae9b2f49">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spod" data-paper-title="Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-spod-93843af2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a42d125f58769f2d">Is a SPOD decision one token or an action of multiple tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspod">Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Protect a full state-conditioned action including native termination, not one token or an episode. Labels are episode-level but protection is decision-specific.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tool name, arguments and terminator form one action within a possibly multi-action success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25034v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a42d125f58769f2d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spod" data-paper-title="Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f73294b40790bec">Why protect full-action probabilities instead of token votes or masking the whole success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspod">Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A specific action in a success is protected when teacher supports it less; probability combines all its tokens. Cancel distillation there and add a soft floor, leaving other actions learnable. Shared parameter changes can still erode protected actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher can like some tool-call tokens and dislike others, so token votes can oppose the whole-call probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25034v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f73294b40790bec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spod" data-paper-title="Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c4645db472f959d">How does a SPOD soft floor differ from masking an entire successful episode?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspod">Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only selected actions are protected; other decisions still distill. A soft penalty below threshold isn&#x27;t a hard guarantee and shared updates can change protected behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One useful successful decision need not block all teacher learning in its episode.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25034v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c4645db472f959d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spod" data-paper-title="Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-afbfefdafb6ba446">Does SPOD compare temperature sampling probability or raw full-action probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspod">Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use raw pre-temperature/pre-constraint probabilities including termination, sum token logp. Recompute gate pre-update but detach it; average by action, state and episode so long traces don&#x27;t dominate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mean token probability isn&#x27;t full-action probability and changes protection by length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25034v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-afbfefdafb6ba446">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:treeopsd" data-paper-title="Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-treeopsd-8a101275" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea2a85257cb9f1bd">Why organize TreeOPSD shared prefixes as a tree?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atreeopsd">Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different continuations from one history reveal outcomes. Back up leaf rewards with behavior likelihood into local credit and count shared turns once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shared first three steps don&#x27;t get duplicated because later branches differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23181v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23181-treeopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea2a85257cb9f1bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:treeopsd" data-paper-title="Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-241ac3d1627b0295">Why convert backed-up tree credit into a bounded Bernoulli target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atreeopsd">Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rewards set direction but no stopping distance. A fixed finite target stops or reverses gradients when reached or exceeded. Deduplicate shared turns and weight branches by full actor-span likelihood, not average token score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeatedly training one success group stops when it has learned enough instead of reinforcing indefinitely.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23181v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23181-treeopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-241ac3d1627b0295">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:treeopsd" data-paper-title="Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-091e270e18989e35">How does bounded Bernoulli teaching differ from repeatedly applying fixed advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atreeopsd">Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frozen posterior gives a finite target: gradient stops at the desired relative change and reverses beyond it. Fixed advantages can keep pushing under repeated updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After sufficient adjustment, stop rather than drive the action farther on the same batch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23181v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23181-treeopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-091e270e18989e35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:treeopsd" data-paper-title="Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dcc62aef7e508b26">Is TreeOPSD&#x27;s Bernoulli a full next-token teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atreeopsd">Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A two-point posterior describes a sampled turn relative to old policy. Use full actor-span likelihood and leaf-reward sample SD, exclude observations, and retain bounded-target derivation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The two outcomes are not two vocabulary tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23181v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23181-treeopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dcc62aef7e508b26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:multiagent-opd" data-paper-title="MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-multiagent-opd-b3177be0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1250f479e1d32a0f">Why train a simple Searcher–Answerer teacher first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amultiagent-opd">MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Team terminal rewards are coarse for search. Train a task-relevant local teacher, then freeze it to guide hierarchical Searcher. Leader and Answerer keep distinct outcome signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Final answer correctness alone can&#x27;t rate the search summary reliably.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23234-multiagent-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1250f479e1d32a0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:multiagent-opd" data-paper-title="MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f609e498e460cc82">Why train a simple teacher but restart the hierarchical student from base?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amultiagent-opd">MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Searcher–Answerer learns local task guidance. Restart distinguishes teacher knowledge from hierarchy learning. Shared weights still receive role-specific signals, and Searcher teacher sees real subtask/history, not global gold for all.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failed answer can reflect delegation or retrieval; uniform terminal credit misses local causes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23234-multiagent-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f609e498e460cc82">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:multiagent-opd" data-paper-title="MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a5c7077c1993896">Why restart phase two from the same base instead of continuing phase one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amultiagent-opd">MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Restart isolates teacher learning from hierarchical student improvement. Shared initialization doesn&#x27;t imply both teacher and student keep updating.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Build a search teacher first, then train a team from base rather than convert teacher weights directly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23234-multiagent-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a5c7077c1993896">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:multiagent-opd" data-paper-title="MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b25f0f6e8f3131c">Do shared MultiAgent parameters still need role-specific loss masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amultiagent-opd">MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Roles use distinct advantages and KL. Searcher log ratio isn&#x27;t causal contribution; mask tool observations. Activity counts environment steps with search, not raw calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiple parallel searches in one step should not inflate leader activity without limit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.23234-multiagent-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1b25f0f6e8f3131c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:waypoint-opd" data-paper-title="Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-waypoint-opd-30b78a3d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-00806496e3e63d41">Why use a waypoint checkpoint from the same teacher RL run?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Awaypoint-opd">Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Endpoints hide reversal. Midpoint shows early/late directional consistency and gates endpoint credit without becoming another imitation target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Monotonic movement toward B and movement toward A then B can end similarly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21601v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21601-waypoint-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-00806496e3e63d41">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:waypoint-opd" data-paper-title="Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f5a0af895743a394">Why use the midpoint as gate rather than a separate target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Awaypoint-opd">Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal endpoint shifts can be consistent or reversed. Compare student-weight-centered early/late directions, then scale endpoint credit only. Freeze gate with low-norm fallback; no requirement to imitate the midpoint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two teachers raise one token eventually, but one first lowers it. Midpoint distinguishes trajectories without teaching that interim state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21601v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21601-waypoint-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f5a0af895743a394">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:waypoint-opd" data-paper-title="Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0952467fc9f0c25">How does positive cosine consistency differ from endpoint magnitude?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Awaypoint-opd">Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Magnitude can hide oscillation. Cosine checks alignment of centered early/late shifts. It is evidence about one training path, not correctness or arbitrary cross-run chronology.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Opposite segments lower gate despite a large final shift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21601v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21601-waypoint-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0952467fc9f0c25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
