<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:waypoint-opd" data-paper-title="Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-df2d02d36c9b2aa5">Why default the waypoint gate to one for tiny norms?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Awaypoint-opd">Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Undefined direction is not conflict. Fall back to one, with student-top-k weighted centering and valid-prefix batch scaling. Freeze support, teacher and advantage. Unsampled candidates may receive gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Near-zero early displacement shouldn&#x27;t delete all endpoint credit because cosine is unstable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21601v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21601-waypoint-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-df2d02d36c9b2aa5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:token-teacher-selection" data-paper-title="Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-token-teacher-selection-efd8fec8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d55cda5621b9a491">Why might selecting teachers tokenwise help compared with one per response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atoken-teacher-selection">Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A response mixes expertise and teacher–student compatibility can vary by prefix. Routing is a plausible mechanism, not a universal empirical win.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Code and math explanations can benefit from different teachers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d55cda5621b9a491">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:token-teacher-selection" data-paper-title="Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f07bd4fdf3bcc63d">Why aren&#x27;t average teacher probabilities and average logits equivalent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atoken-teacher-selection">Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Arithmetic mixes allocate mass across distributions; log averaging and normalization favor shared support, particularly under tail/mode disagreement. Confidence, distance and aligned features are distinct criteria without universally optimal routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Math/code experts can favor different continuations; sharing their mass differs from requiring common support.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f07bd4fdf3bcc63d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:token-teacher-selection" data-paper-title="Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6832747bbabf135">What assumptions underlie confidence, Hellinger and hidden-distance routing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atoken-teacher-selection">Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Confidence values certainty, distribution distance values compatibility, and hidden distance requires aligned representations. They measure different properties; unequal dimensions can&#x27;t be subtracted, and closeness isn&#x27;t correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A confident teacher far beyond student skill may receive different weights by rule.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6832747bbabf135">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:token-teacher-selection" data-paper-title="Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e36bfbfb2f297f76">Does soft teacher routing mix probabilities or logits, and what if τ=0?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atoken-teacher-selection">Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Arithmetic mix probabilities; averaged logits give a geometric target. τ=0 uses hard argmax. Freeze routing/target. Local sampled-token path is not Top-K KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different teacher modes get different mass under probability and logit mixtures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e36bfbfb2f297f76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tf-opd" data-paper-title="Training-Free On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tf-opd-c139b549" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0898ca99dc7454b0">Why does training-free TF-OPD still need teacher-generated data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atf-opd">Training-Free On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Closed-form linear merging uses input second moments from each teacher&#x27;s visited states to determine output matching. No gradients does not mean no generation or calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two specialists&#x27; statistics reveal different input subspaces.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22236-tf-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0898ca99dc7454b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tf-opd" data-paper-title="Training-Free On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c2ec17d36f032bf9">Why use teacher-specific input second moments rather than a shared covariance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atf-opd">Training-Free On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They weight output error along actually visited directions. Arbitrary shared statistics change least squares; termination filtering and token normalization matter. Gradient-free still costs generation, rescoring and solving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One shared covariance may ignore the domain-specific support of one expert.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22236-tf-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c2ec17d36f032bf9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tf-opd" data-paper-title="Training-Free On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6678e5697a58a0f">How does equal-Gram merging differ from summing task vectors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atf-opd">Training-Free On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Identical Gram statistics should yield a weighted average, not amplified sum. Orthogonal support can preserve separate functions. Behavior depends on statistics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two identical experts should not produce twice the task update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22236-tf-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6678e5697a58a0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tf-opd" data-paper-title="Training-Free On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-40ed8419c11180ff">Whose responses estimate TF-OPD Grams?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atf-opd">Training-Free On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each teacher rescores its own responses after termination/loop filtering; normalize by tokens. Use FP64 linear solves, not explicit inverse, and clean hooks. Random covariance isn&#x27;t teacher evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring student-generated text changes teacher visitation statistics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22236-tf-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40ed8419c11180ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:shared-residual-distillation" data-paper-title="Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-shared-residual-distillation-a834c6f2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2437a16c7225567d">Why not choose an SRD answer by majority vote?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ashared-residual-distillation">Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unverified peers can all be wrong yet contain useful local signals. Compare same-question peers with cross-question controls; retain minimum common signed residual instead of declaring a whole answer correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failed traces can still share one reasonable intermediate step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22080v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22080-shared-residual-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2437a16c7225567d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:shared-residual-distillation" data-paper-title="Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb763df961ba8600">Why retain minimum same-sign peer residual without selecting one whole answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ashared-residual-distillation">Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare same-question changes to control to isolate local task effects. Conservative common magnitudes limit individual overreach. Student sees only own prefix; agreement is not truth and target cannot reinforce itself as a peer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep a weakly supported common middle word without declaring an unverified conclusion correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22080v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22080-shared-residual-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb763df961ba8600">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:shared-residual-distillation" data-paper-title="Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc3074a967131230">How does minmod residual differ from averaging peer logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ashared-residual-distillation">Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep the minimum magnitude only when all signs agree; otherwise zero. Mean can let strong opinions swamp conflict. Shared agreement can still be biased.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two positive peers and one negative don&#x27;t get a positive residual by simple majority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22080v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22080-shared-residual-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc3074a967131230">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:shared-residual-distillation" data-paper-title="Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f73fc7a75f99e03">Why can an SRD coordinate-capped surrogate be negative?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ashared-residual-distillation">Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It caps signed coordinate contributions, not total KL. Use q0 centering weights, exclude target from its peers and freeze teachers/targets. Clamping negative coordinates changes the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A negative local coordinate may be valid even when a KL interpretation concerns the full distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd-reminder" data-paper-title="OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-oprd-reminder-a48a675d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2796add4208606d">Why sample reminder-OPRD students without reminders?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd-reminder">OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deployment is unhinted. After failure a privileged teacher rescores actual prefixes using reminders to internalize constraints. Successful traces use self-imitation rather than teacher rewrites.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A missed testing constraint can guide training scoring while inference sees only original task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21496v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21496-oprd-reminder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2796add4208606d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd-reminder" data-paper-title="OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-03709a88439f630e">Why expire OPRD local reminders after the relevant next turn?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd-reminder">OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A specific observation triggers a short-lived constraint. Global/local scopes differ; teacher rescores actual prefixes and deployment receives no reminder. Normalize success imitation and failure distillation separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A dependency reminder from compilation should expire after the dependency is fixed, not remain pending forever.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21496v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21496-oprd-reminder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-03709a88439f630e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd-reminder" data-paper-title="OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-48dbec89ac3890dd">How do global and post-observation local reminder scopes differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd-reminder">OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global reminders persist; local ones apply only to the next turn after that observation and then expire. Permanent local reminders change unrelated conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fix for one error belongs to the next attempt, not every later turn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21496v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21496-oprd-reminder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48dbec89ac3890dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd-reminder" data-paper-title="OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d293ce6549e892f4">How choose reminder-OPRD Top-100 and refresh teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd-reminder">OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rank shared support by elementwise max of both logp vectors, then normalize each on it. Refresh teacher at specified milestones, otherwise freeze. Average each trace then success/failure separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Independent supports compare different events in coordinatewise KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21496v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21496-oprd-reminder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d293ce6549e892f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:elite-replay" data-paper-title="EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-elite-replay-bbf50043" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-efb23a3165472dcb">Why maintain a quality–diversity archive per EliteReplay problem?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aelite-replay">EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accuracy alone can shrink solution coverage. Keep the shortest verified solution per approach/structure cell to preserve distinct successful strategies rather than store ordinary IID replay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Separate algebra and geometry cells so the common strategy doesn&#x27;t overwrite the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22290v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22290-elite-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efb23a3165472dcb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:elite-replay" data-paper-title="EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7b4a830107e28f1">Why index EliteReplay by realized approach and balance problem before cell?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aelite-replay">EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Requested methods can differ from generated ones. Use actual descriptor and retain shortest verified answer in each cell. Problem-first balancing prevents archive size from allocating weight. This isn&#x27;t IID success caching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A requested geometry solution using algebra belongs in algebra, or identical methods masquerade as diversity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22290v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22290-elite-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7b4a830107e28f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:elite-replay" data-paper-title="EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b2ee625f7485ad7">How does shortest-per-cell MAP-Elites differ from a global shortest answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aelite-replay">EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cell-local replacement preserves other strategies. Store actual descriptors, not requested approaches, which may not match generated behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A proof requested as induction but generated by enumeration belongs to the enumeration cell.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22290v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22290-elite-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b2ee625f7485ad7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:elite-replay" data-paper-title="EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a6a4358f1278fa3">Why balance problems before occupied cells?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aelite-replay">EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise larger archives dominate replay. Average response tokens, mix archive and GRPO as specified, clear padding before exponentiating and use no test gold for archiving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>More occupied cells should not give one problem ten times the sampling weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22290v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.22290-elite-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a6a4358f1278fa3">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cce-opd" data-paper-title="Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-cce-opd-2c59e40e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1d96269c32db7e5">Why mask a valid premise in CCE&#x27;s teacher contrast?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acce-opd">Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A teacher may follow a mistaken student prefix instead of using conditions. Matched ablation reveals condition-sensitive directions for an extrapolated auxiliary target. Student always sees the full problem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing a numerical premise can identify which next tokens depend on it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21195v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21195-cce-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c1d96269c32db7e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cce-opd" data-paper-title="Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0a63178fb77e7a3">Why match student prefixes across views and keep full student normalization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acce-opd">Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed prefixes isolate premise removal. Teacher auxiliary target is normalized on candidate support but student uses full-vocabulary softmax, retaining outside gradients. Gate controls only auxiliary correction; base OPD stays.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If premise and student reasoning both change, likelihood differences can&#x27;t isolate the premise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21195v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21195-cce-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0a63178fb77e7a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cce-opd" data-paper-title="Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e02added51ca60cf">Does disabling CCE auxiliary gating remove all OPD at a position?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acce-opd">Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Sampled PPO-OPD remains; only auxiliary forward KL is removed. Premise eligibility and entropy gate the extra term.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A low-entropy format token still receives base distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21195v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21195-cce-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e02added51ca60cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cce-opd" data-paper-title="Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-102d02cb6b593399">Where is CCE entropy computed, and is student renormalized on support?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acce-opd">Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute entropy on full teacher vocabulary before top-set union. Normalize auxiliary target within support but preserve student full softmax for outside-support gradients. Denominator counts all valid positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student support renormalization would hide outside mass and change loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21195v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21195-cce-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-102d02cb6b593399">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rshd" data-paper-title="Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rshd-81aa0b1d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7d54bb36f3dc30d">Why require note-induced replays to improve RSHD pass rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arshd">Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Plausible reflection may not improve behavior. Independently resample and accept only strict improvement over original group, then distill new continuations rather than old failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A note suggesting unit checks is rejected if retries still all fail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21018-rshd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7d54bb36f3dc30d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rshd" data-paper-title="Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-40c22840ad00279a">Why generate fresh replays and require improvement rather than distill old failures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arshd">Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verify the note with actual new behavior and a strict pass-rate gain. Uniformly sample accepted replays and compare note/no-note positive lift on identical prefixes. Old failures aren&#x27;t fixed by explanation; no gold in notes and no auxiliary term without acceptance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A convincing postmortem with all-failed new attempts is not valid teacher guidance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21018-rshd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40c22840ad00279a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rshd" data-paper-title="Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5feccb4a3af77e50">How does uniform replay selection differ from keeping successes only?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arshd">Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uniform selection preserves the note-induced distribution. Success-only conditions on outcomes a second time after note-level gating and changes provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An accepted replay group can include failures; don&#x27;t silently retain only the correct answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21018-rshd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5feccb4a3af77e50">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rshd" data-paper-title="Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-27d881c9240abcc4">Do zero-lift RSHD tokens count in the auxiliary denominator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arshd">Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Count all valid accepted replay tokens, including zeros. No accepted note gives exactly zero auxiliary loss. Detach teacher/lift and never construct notes from gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Dividing only by positive-lift count would overamplify sparse weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21018-rshd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27d881c9240abcc4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:loopsd" data-paper-title="LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-loopsd-e562cd53" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bac65d4d7df1a33">Why create LoOPSD teachers by repeating layers rather than using bigger weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aloopsd">LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anhui Province Key Laboratory of Digital Security</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared parameters can compute a better distribution through a longer loop. Search contiguous repeat regions and distill on student prefixes. Extra compute, not external answers, supplies guidance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeating middle layers changes per-token computation without adding parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18162">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.18162-loopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bac65d4d7df1a33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:loopsd" data-paper-title="LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-54a2b1d469f3558f">Why does repeated-layer LoOPSD cost compute and need validation route selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aloopsd">LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anhui Province Key Laboratory of Digital Security</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Loops change distribution without new weights but execute more layers per token and search multiple routes. Select validation improvements over standard route, then distill student prefixes; never choose on test. More compute doesn&#x27;t guarantee gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rereading a chapter may help but takes time; choose using practice tasks, not final exam answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18162">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.18162-loopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54a2b1d469f3558f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:loopsd" data-paper-title="LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec091fc879a2e050">How does re-searching loops each round differ from a fixed initial loop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aloopsd">LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anhui Province Key Laboratory of Digital Security</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student updates can change useful repeat regions. Search adapts, and continue only if independent validation beats standard routing, not test-selected routes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A useful repeated middle region can stop helping after the student learns it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18162">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.18162-loopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec091fc879a2e050">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:loopsd" data-paper-title="LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c26a3bcf42e94a53">Do teacher weights/routes get gradients during LoOPSD distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aloopsd">LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anhui Province Key Laboratory of Digital Security</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freeze both for the round; update standard student via RKL. Training references can be used only for permitted route search, not student rollout. Count repeated-layer compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five repeated layers are not free even without new parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18162">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.18162-loopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c26a3bcf42e94a53">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:road-mopd" data-paper-title="Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-road-mopd-dfda03a0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d72be295b3638f74">Why query unrouted teachers in Road-MOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroad-mopd">Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared parameters can degrade other domains even if examples route separately. Evaluate other teachers on the same prefixes for compatibility and real auxiliary gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Math updates can affect code behavior despite separate data routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13521">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13521-road-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d72be295b3638f74">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:road-mopd" data-paper-title="Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-71c3912df71c02aa">Why use unrouted teachers and impose a target gradient norm floor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroad-mopd">Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Auxiliary teachers check cross-domain harm on identical states. Gate token credit, then address real gradient conflicts without overweakening target learning. Norm floors are tradeoffs, not universal gains; arbitrary vectors don&#x27;t replace objectives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Code guidance can protect prefixes during math updates, but full removal might stall math learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13521">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13521-road-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-71c3912df71c02aa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:road-mopd" data-paper-title="Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ffa58a5632fef07f">Can Road token gating replace gradient projection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroad-mopd">Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Gating scales local supervision; projection handles shared-parameter conflict with a target norm floor. A weight formula isn&#x27;t the complete mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compatible scores do not rule out gradient conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13521">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13521-road-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ffa58a5632fef07f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:road-mopd" data-paper-title="Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2aa17d83bd77ca58">Why not remove the entire conflicting component in Road projection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroad-mopd">Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choose maximum feasible projection while preserving the target norm floor; full projection can violate it. Compute actual auxiliary gradients, not static scores or registry labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Near antiparallel gradients can make a fully projected update vanish.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13521">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13521-road-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2aa17d83bd77ca58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cast-opd" data-paper-title="CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-cast-opd-cae7ae27" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-da0704fa87323c6b">Why align decoded spans for cross-tokenizer CAST?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acast-opd">CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token IDs and boundaries differ. Match equivalent decoded spans, then project teacher span logp into student positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two Chinese tokenizations may split a word differently but decode to the same span.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13257-cast-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da0704fa87323c6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cast-opd" data-paper-title="CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f5504a33d943aad">Why align decoded spans before projecting teacher log probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acast-opd">CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Position-wise IDs lack a common event. Verified text spans provide corresponding regions, then uncertainty/smoothness allocate conserved credit. Anchor unmatched text and disclose alignment gaps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one teacher token becomes several student tokens, verify identical decoded span before allocating its score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13257-cast-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f5504a33d943aad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cast-opd" data-paper-title="CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b1393548f9b6b374">How does CAST allocation differ from CSD shared events?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acast-opd">CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CAST distributes total teacher span credit over student positions. CSD builds common-event probability distributions with REST. They conserve different objects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Conserving one span&#x27;s advantage is not preserving all event probability mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13257-cast-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b1393548f9b6b374">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cast-opd" data-paper-title="CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cac37d3cbe163f6b">How does CAST uncertainty weighting preserve chunk credit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acast-opd">CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize weights from uncertainty and local smoothness, then multiply chunk total advantage. Anchor unmatched positions to initial student rather than drop them and claim full coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A higher token share must not increase total chunk advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13257-cast-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cac37d3cbe163f6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sguid" data-paper-title="Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sguid-340394af" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ff07f5766fc4cbf">Why measure sustained teaching activity rather than similarity in SGUID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asguid">Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Relevant skills can teach poorly. Generate from verified traces and check early/late persistence and verifier agreement. Retrieval frequency isn&#x27;t useful teaching count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A frequently retrieved but misleading skill shouldn&#x27;t stay because it looks relevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12367">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.12367-sguid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ff07f5766fc4cbf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sguid" data-paper-title="Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a83dcc5631e0862a">Why restore round-start weights and retrain only selected skills?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asguid">Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise broad probe exposure confounds the compact curriculum effect. Reset, train selected skills, and regenerate from the updated model next round. Count sustained verifier-aligned teaching, not semantic matches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Testing ten hints gives extra practice; without a reset, later gain can&#x27;t be assigned to the two selected hints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12367">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.12367-sguid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a83dcc5631e0862a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sguid" data-paper-title="Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-97c4c173d0fb5f4f">Why restore initial round weights after SGUID probing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asguid">Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probes already update the model. Restore to isolate training with compact selected library from extra probe learning. Next round generates new skills, not a fixed manual archive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Continuing after probing all candidates would retain discarded skills&#x27; effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12367">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.12367-sguid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97c4c173d0fb5f4f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sguid" data-paper-title="Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ca77e8fe6c1a39f">May SGUID delete negative coefficients, and how should negative results be handled?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asguid">Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The objective allows negative teaching signals. Check early/late activity and quality. Validation decline after two executed rounds remains a negative result, not success because the loop ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Early gains don&#x27;t justify retention if late signals fall below thresholds.</p>
