<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12367">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.12367-sguid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ca77e8fe6c1a39f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:meta-opd" data-paper-title="MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-meta-opd-c3af9659" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-385bc0a690ca1ca8">Why learn MetaOPD weights through a virtual student step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ameta-opd">MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher gap does not reveal which signals improve tasks. Evaluate virtual updates against training-reference loss, use meta-gradients to learn weighting, then update the student with new weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A large gap on a token may harm the reference task and deserve lower weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11989-meta-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-385bc0a690ca1ca8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:meta-opd" data-paper-title="MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3cd49e2f1d4159d">Why need a differentiable virtual update instead of weighting by current loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ameta-opd">MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High loss can be noise. A virtual step reveals downstream reference-loss effects and meta-gradients, then real student update uses learned weights. Isolate descriptors, optimizer state and training-only references.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare whether emphasizing a stylistic high-loss word or a reasoning token better serves the reference task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11989-meta-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3cd49e2f1d4159d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:meta-opd" data-paper-title="MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6660a79840557aed">How does differentiable virtual AdamW differ from scoring an actual step afterward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ameta-opd">MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Virtual step retains the graph to weight network for meta-gradients, while real update mutates state without that derivative. Optimizer state/order matter; arbitrary SGD isn&#x27;t equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ask how weights caused the hypothetical change, not only whether a metric changed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11989-meta-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6660a79840557aed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:meta-opd" data-paper-title="MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-081c80386f8001e6">What detaches in MetaOPD&#x27;s 74-dimensional descriptors and weight transform?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ameta-opd">MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Detach descriptors, not the weight network through the virtual step. Center per response, bound via tanh and normalize to mean one. Use new weights for real update; references come from allowed training data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Test references cannot supervise outer-loop weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11989-meta-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-081c80386f8001e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:where-opd" data-paper-title="Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-where-opd-73f1d45e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0798f7dbc5e175d">Why use synthetic scene coordinates as privileged Where-OPD input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Awhere-opd">Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Valeo.ai</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generated scenes provide exact objects/positions for teacher while student sees image/question. Internalize spatial hints without coordinate access at deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher knows positions; student learns left/right from pixels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02117">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.02117-where-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0798f7dbc5e175d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:where-opd" data-paper-title="Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4a2e2a2808d8743">Why give teacher textual coordinates while student receives only image and question?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Awhere-opd">Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Valeo.ai</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exact synthetic object/location metadata gives privileged scoring on student prefixes. Deployment lacks that metadata, so keep student inputs clean. Preserve spatial mask; random-logit tests don&#x27;t prove spatial ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher can correct left-of-box relationships, but test students cannot be told coordinates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02117">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.02117-where-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4a2e2a2808d8743">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:where-opd" data-paper-title="Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6e6be5151119ef4">How does spatial privileged text differ from ordinary text distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Awhere-opd">Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Valeo.ai</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The method needs matching actual scene images and spatial annotations. Random text distributions don&#x27;t verify visual integration; privilege doesn&#x27;t prove student reliance on images.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct description paired with the wrong image still yields a computable loss but meaningless guidance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02117">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.02117-where-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6e6be5151119ef4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:where-opd" data-paper-title="Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d953d9a8ea49d645">Does local Where-OPD generate scenes and load an MLLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Awhere-opd">Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Valeo.ai</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks teacher KL under a spatial mask aligned to generated student positions, with frozen teacher. Random logits aren&#x27;t visual evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two hand-built left/right logits don&#x27;t constitute image reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02117">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.02117-where-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d953d9a8ea49d645">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weakest-link" data-paper-title="The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-weakest-link-b901a370" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c7bd5b0d985d1030">Why require every prefix to satisfy average cost in Weakest Link?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweakest-link">The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A final mean can hide bad early reasoning diluted by easy later tokens. First violation is absorbing. Costs are teacher negative logp.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Appending common words cannot undo an unsupported prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00332-weakest-link/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c7bd5b0d985d1030">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weakest-link" data-paper-title="The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7923acb97ed47a03">Why does an early violation persist instead of being diluted by easy later tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweakest-link">The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Every prefix must meet teacher cost. Absorption blocks post hoc dilution; immediate counterfactuals vary only action at the real visited prefix. Teacher improbability still doesn&#x27;t prove factual error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding common words after an unsupported derivation may lower final cost but cannot satisfy already violated prefixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00332-weakest-link/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7923acb97ed47a03">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weakest-link" data-paper-title="The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-51efc32637c1fc66">How does absorbing penalty differ from a recoverable moving gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweakest-link">The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Violation persists even if later average improves. A rolling gate might reopen. This is a prefix constraint, not proof teacher cost equals task value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One high-probability next token doesn&#x27;t clear the previous violation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00332-weakest-link/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51efc32637c1fc66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weakest-link" data-paper-title="The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-18fe7c725ef08fd9">May counterfactual current actions use different historical costs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweakest-link">The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Start from actual prefix cost and vary only current action. Exact full-vocabulary immediate gradients coexist with sampled future returns. No full LM trainer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Inventing a worse history for an unfavored action invalidates its comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00332-weakest-link/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18fe7c725ef08fd9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pr-opd" data-paper-title="PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-pr-opd-9c73d4f9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-59a45194479a55f0">Why distill representations in PR-OPD rather than only final probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apr-opd">PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hindsight skills create privileged hidden states. Align projected states at matching layers and response positions, then combine with task reward. Teacher skill is removed at inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A retrospective tool principle can guide internal features without being deployment input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36642-pr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-59a45194479a55f0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pr-opd" data-paper-title="PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ceecfd34d31cf4a4">Why forward the same response with/without hindsight skill rather than imitate skill text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apr-opd">PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare how skill changes same-token/layer representations and transfer to an unprivileged student. Copying skill or teacher replies changes targets. Detach teacher, combine task reward and remove privilege at inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher can rescore an earlier decision using a validation reminder that the deployed student never sees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36642-pr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ceecfd34d31cf4a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pr-opd" data-paper-title="PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5d6558b0b26dd06">How do two forwards differ from concatenating skill to student context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apr-opd">PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Run ordinary student and privileged detached teacher separately. Giving student skill changes deployment assumptions and can teach dependency. Representation matching isn&#x27;t answer supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tested student should rely on learned parameters when no skill text is supplied.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36642-pr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5d6558b0b26dd06">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pr-opd" data-paper-title="PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ed3d42bb6433d2a">What masks apply to layerwise PR-OPD alignment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apr-opd">PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Align valid tokens of the same response at corresponding layers, excluding observations/padding. Skills come from completed training traces, not gold plans. Local kernel isn&#x27;t agent training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not align extra teacher skill tokens to student response positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36642-pr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ed3d42bb6433d2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:maestro-opd" data-paper-title="From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-maestro-opd-551f210d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3338a9b96bec70e1">Why intervene only at MAESTRO&#x27;s high-disagreement prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amaestro-opd">From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher rollouts are expensive. Top-k coverage, similarity and early-position weighting allocate limited guidance. Disagreement doesn&#x27;t automatically mean student error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An early fork can matter more than a punctuation discrepancy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37510">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37510-maestro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3338a9b96bec70e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:maestro-opd" data-paper-title="From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d66864e0fc2fc51c">Why use both top-k coverage and Bhattacharyya similarity for interventions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amaestro-opd">From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One checks support inclusion, the other shared probability allocation. Disagreement and position weight prioritize scarce teacher compute. It is a clue, not correctness; local PDS doesn&#x27;t generate a takeover.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two models can share identical top-k words while assigning very different probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37510">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37510-maestro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d66864e0fc2fc51c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:maestro-opd" data-paper-title="From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2d65dccc35ab4180">Why combine coverage and Bhattacharyya similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amaestro-opd">From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coverage checks whether student candidates include teacher support. Similarity compares mass within shared support. Either alone misses differences; high PDS isn&#x27;t teacher correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical candidates can have almost opposite weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37510">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37510-maestro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2d65dccc35ab4180">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:maestro-opd" data-paper-title="From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d5b4623fbf3f723">Does local MAESTRO generate takeover rollouts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amaestro-opd">From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It computes top-k coverage, normalized similarity and PDS. Real intervention needs generation, state handoff and cost accounting; no measured call savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Hand-entered probabilities can trigger a score without any teacher rollout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37510">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37510-maestro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d5b4623fbf3f723">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lego-opd" data-paper-title="LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-lego-opd-93f05fa7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d289372d6af6441f">Can LEGO-OPD grounding likelihood be read as the final answer probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alego-opd">LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is the visual evidence factor, combined with language prior and normalized. Distinguish prior, likelihood and final posterior, not interpret one score as answer confidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Vision supports red; language constrains valid next words. Combine and normalize for token probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00333-lego-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d289372d6af6441f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lego-opd" data-paper-title="LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0be0a85b3520122d">Why combine a language prior and visual likelihood instead of averaging teachers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alego-opd">LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Language supplies general grammar/reasoning while vision modifies evidence through a product. This can avoid copying visual model language bias if its likelihood is reliable. Local target checks do not prove vision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Language makes a cup description grammatical; visual evidence increases the color it shows.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00333-lego-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0be0a85b3520122d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lego-opd" data-paper-title="LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-16ed41f70e40a9e1">How does setting grounding α=0 differ from using only vision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alego-opd">LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A valid zero-weight visual contribution leaves language prior. Vision-only would remove language, a different target. α scales evidence, not votes between two complete models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiplying visual log contribution by zero leaves language scores, not pure vision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00333-lego-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16ed41f70e40a9e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lego-opd" data-paper-title="LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d2bbd06c7f56d04">Does local LEGO load both language and visual experts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alego-opd">LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It only combines factors. Align candidates, add in log space, then normalize. Visual likelihood isn&#x27;t a full VLM posterior; random logits aren&#x27;t visual capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiplying two vectors doesn&#x27;t make any model see an image.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.00333-lego-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d2bbd06c7f56d04">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:advisd" data-paper-title="AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-advisd-0fd17b91" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9689d817dbfc3cb9">Why train AdviSD advisor and freeze executor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadvisd">AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Improve advice to a fixed strong executor, isolating advisor contribution. Reflection generates candidate advice; only advice affecting executor preferences enough enters self-distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Improve parameter-check reminders without changing the tool model weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38142">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.38142-advisd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9689d817dbfc3cb9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:advisd" data-paper-title="AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6de6ac398dbe65f4">Why score a fixed executor reply in both advice conditions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadvisd">AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed reply controls generation randomness and isolates preference shift. Train advisor on threshold-passing reflections while executor stays frozen. A likelihood increase isn&#x27;t task success and calibration depends on advice distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rescore the same recorded tool call in both contexts rather than subtract independently generated answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38142">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.38142-advisd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6de6ac398dbe65f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:advisd" data-paper-title="AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f29a6d7748aa8d87">Is influential advice necessarily successful advice?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadvisd">AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Likelihood contrast measures preference shifts on one recorded response. Donor calibration screens weak effects, not whether the change improves outcomes; evaluate tasks separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Advice can increase support for an existing wrong action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38142">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.38142-advisd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f29a6d7748aa8d87">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:advisd" data-paper-title="AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f3d700f9d4b64e0">May AdviSD generate separate replies for with/without advice comparisons?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadvisd">AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not in place of paired rescoring. Use the same response and mean valid-token logp; threshold from donor absolute contrast quantile. No local real executor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different newly generated long and short answers confound advice effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38142">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.38142-advisd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f3d700f9d4b64e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:olive" data-paper-title="Learning from Teacher Continuations at Student States" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-olive-4870752f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-be7936ba40a16330">Why let OLIVE teacher continue from student-visited states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aolive">Learning from Teacher Continuations at Student States</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student mistakes differ from ideal teacher paths. Real prefixes supply deployment-like supervision for continuation/recovery instead of memorizing complete solutions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Continue from an unusual intermediate expression the student reached.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36246">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36246-olive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be7936ba40a16330">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:olive" data-paper-title="Learning from Teacher Continuations at Student States" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d5768797235694a">Why don&#x27;t OLIVE prefixes receive supervised loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aolive">Learning from Teacher Continuations at Student States</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher continues the student&#x27;s actual prefix, giving useful next-step examples without treating student mistakes as correct labels. Apply CE only to teacher tokens. Teacher quality and full-model experiments remain separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Read a repairable wrong expression and learn only the corrected teacher continuation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36246">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36246-olive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d5768797235694a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:olive" data-paper-title="Learning from Teacher Continuations at Student States" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-648e9cd502b8ce7a">How does teacher continuation CE differ from scoring original student tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aolive">Learning from Teacher Continuations at Student States</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuation adds newly generated teacher text as target; rescoring evaluates existing sampled actions/states. A scoring kernel doesn&#x27;t produce new teacher continuations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Writing the next steps differs from rating the old steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36246">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36246-olive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-648e9cd502b8ce7a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:olive" data-paper-title="Learning from Teacher Continuations at Student States" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-af1bd061756a9659">Can OLIVE remove prefixes from input because they have no loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aolive">Learning from Teacher Continuations at Student States</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Prefix remains conditioning for continuation and student supervision; mask targets only. Handle concatenation, EOS and padding. Local tests verify masks without a closed teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retain three mistaken steps as context without training to imitate them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36246">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.36246-olive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af1bd061756a9659">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mas-opd" data-paper-title="MAS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mas-opd-e3c3be86" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ff54511f31821a3">Why add role-specific advantage in MAS-OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amas-opd">MAS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal team outcomes hide member responsibility. Target vs other-role teacher signals supply local collaboration credit. Verify attribution rather than punish everyone equally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Good retrieval and faulty summarization call for different credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.34234-mas-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ff54511f31821a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mas-opd" data-paper-title="MAS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1042ce3ff30e42a">Why put conflict attribution in teacher view instead of changing every role&#x27;s reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amas-opd">MAS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One team score doesn&#x27;t identify corrections. Privileged teacher distinguishes target and other contributions. Extra attribution is training-only and local mask/advantage does not establish multi-model collaboration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sound planner and an executor using the wrong tool shouldn&#x27;t receive the same blame.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.34234-mas-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1042ce3ff30e42a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mas-opd" data-paper-title="MAS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ff64018a557f657">How does teacher-only conflict information differ from giving full attribution to all roles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amas-opd">MAS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Students act on their own public histories; only teacher sees extra conflict explanation. Giving hindsight to students changes deployment inputs and hides whether learning internalized it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher may know who misunderstood after failure; deployed members cannot start with that diagnosis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.34234-mas-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ff64018a557f657">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mas-opd" data-paper-title="MAS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a2f647ebe9aace5">Does local MAS-OPD jointly train real models?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amas-opd">MAS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It tests role advantage and conflict masks. Align roles, traces and valid generated positions. Registry labels or misassigned signals don&#x27;t establish team training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapping role order can keep arrays valid while assigning credit to the wrong member.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.34234-mas-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a2f647ebe9aace5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-aha" data-paper-title="OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opd-aha-11a1ffc3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2931ec0c204282a6">What does language inertia mean in OPD-Aha?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-aha">OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University / University of Virginia / Stevens Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A wrong student prefix can lead a teacher to keep repeating it despite visual evidence. Compare actual and empty vision to recover visual contributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If prior text says dog and picture shows cat, don&#x27;t blindly continue dog.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16459">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16459-opd-aha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2931ec0c204282a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-aha" data-paper-title="OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4be5a9972445c455">Why compare teacher distributions with real and empty visual input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-aha">OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University / University of Virginia / Stevens Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The comparison isolates preference changes attributable to image conditioning despite mistaken text context. It helps separate evidence from prior but doesn&#x27;t guarantee correctness. Local evidence is reconstruction only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A cat image can shift preferences away from the prefix&#x27;s dog claim relative to no vision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16459">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16459-opd-aha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4be5a9972445c455">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-aha" data-paper-title="OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ffb8e96a88323b0c">How does real/empty vision contrast differ from raising confidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-aha">OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University / University of Virginia / Stevens Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It changes vision while matching teacher context. Sharpening can amplify language priors. Empty-view design and teacher quality affect attribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If both views confidently say dog, sharpening won&#x27;t discover the cat.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16459">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16459-opd-aha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ffb8e96a88323b0c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-aha" data-paper-title="OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a9393dd8b5eedad">Does local OPD-Aha reconstruction use a multimodal checkpoint?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-aha">OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University / University of Virginia / Stevens Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It tests target math. Real implementation needs paired visual/empty inputs and identical student prefixes scored by a model. Fixed differences don&#x27;t establish visual reflection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Manually increasing cat probability checks reconstruction, not image recognition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16459">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16459-opd-aha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a9393dd8b5eedad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:nsd" data-paper-title="Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-nsd-9169c0f1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-156313e8fb4c0f9c">Why use self-generated mistakes as negative teaching material in NSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ansd">Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Failures identify directions to avoid. Negative teacher models error distribution and a dynamic gate concentrates suppression on key reasoning while protecting ordinary language.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A misused proof rule can supply an avoid signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11699">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11699-nsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-156313e8fb4c0f9c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:nsd" data-paper-title="Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7073cf71d4eaf23">Why not suppress the entire erroneous answer in NSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ansd">Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Negative teacher gives a distribution to avoid, with dynamic gates selecting reasoning-critical tokens while preserving useful language/steps. Selection doesn&#x27;t prove errors and full LM training wasn&#x27;t reproduced.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A carry error needn&#x27;t suppress every connective and correct digit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11699">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11699-nsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7073cf71d4eaf23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:nsd" data-paper-title="Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-886ee3b24ca799ed">How does negative self-distillation differ from lowering every wrong answer token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ansd">Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Wrong responses can contain valid facts, grammar and steps. Selective gating limits collateral damage, but isn&#x27;t a verified step label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A wrong result doesn&#x27;t mean all numbers and connectives should be forgotten.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11699">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11699-nsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-886ee3b24ca799ed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:nsd" data-paper-title="Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fdf24dcd2d314d24">What supplies local NSD negative teachers and gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Ansd">Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidate policies test control flow, not full-parameter LLM. Freeze and align gates to penalized positions; test gold cannot preidentify errors under no-leakage claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Hand-labeled errors are a unit fixture, not autonomous error localization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11699">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11699-nsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fdf24dcd2d314d24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compass-opd" data-paper-title="CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-compass-opd-6b3a07da" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-569a9735016a2295">Why does CompassOPD need each teacher&#x27;s own reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompass-opd">CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Absolute probability scales differ across families. Relative change captures post-training direction, and within-family centering reduces global bias before using the student anchor. It isn&#x27;t correctness proof.</p>
