<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A naturally sharp teacher shouldn&#x27;t look more learned just because probabilities are larger.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10154">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.10154-compass-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-569a9735016a2295">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compass-opd" data-paper-title="CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4e800f5f08e0695">Why compare post-trained teacher to its own reference rather than absolute teacher–student scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompass-opd">CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calibration and sharpness vary by family. Relative likelihood shifts and within-family centering extract direction, with a student reference anchor. Teacher bias can remain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two teachers may both increasingly favor the right step despite very different initial distributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10154">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.10154-compass-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4e800f5f08e0695">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compass-opd" data-paper-title="CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-687df570b70d35ac">How does Compass trade off against averaging cross-family probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompass-opd">CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Relative directions mitigate scale effects but discard some global information. Direct mixtures retain absolute posteriors. Compare under equal protocol; no universal win.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two moves toward the correct option shouldn&#x27;t be obscured by native temperature differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10154">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.10154-compass-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-687df570b70d35ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compass-opd" data-paper-title="CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1ec49abd65dc106">What comparable sets should Compass center over?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompass-opd">CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use consistent candidates/weights for specified family changes and a separate student reference. Don&#x27;t center arbitrarily across questions. Local audit magnitudes aren&#x27;t training success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mismatched option order makes subtraction meaningless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10154">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.10154-compass-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1ec49abd65dc106">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd" data-paper-title="Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-oprd-e69b9862" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-349513728ef75b89">What information transfers from weak to strong in OPRD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd">Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weak post-training logit change relative to base augments strong verifier gradient. Weak answers needn&#x27;t outperform strong ones; a useful update direction may transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A learned unit-check tendency can help without copying weak arithmetic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08798">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.08798-oprd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-349513728ef75b89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd" data-paper-title="Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-960ba50ff9253e9e">Why transfer weak-model direction without asking the strong model to imitate answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd">Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extract centered normalized weak-after/base difference and boost aligned strong-verifier components. The transfer object is direction, not content. Utility requires alignment and candidate diagnostics don&#x27;t prove broad gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A stronger model can learn to check units without copying an incorrect weak numeric result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08798">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.08798-oprd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-960ba50ff9253e9e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd" data-paper-title="Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-761aac5efd4bbe26">How does OPRD gradient augmentation differ from full weak-teacher distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd">Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep strong verifier gradient and amplify its component along weak learning direction, instead of fitting weak distribution. An irrelevant direction may not help.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Strong model still follows its reward with directional modulation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08798">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.08798-oprd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-761aac5efd4bbe26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd" data-paper-title="Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e39f4f113b3c46a3">How handle zero change and gradient direction in OPRD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd">Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Center and unit-normalize deltas; treat zero norm as no direction. Add projection to original gradient, not replace it. Local candidates only map the proxy to parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical weak checkpoints should not generate a divide-by-zero teaching direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08798">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.08798-oprd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e39f4f113b3c46a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weak-guide-rlvr" data-paper-title="Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-weak-guide-rlvr-a37f47f8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18d555967dc0fe5d">Why can weak-model prefixes improve strong exploration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweak-guide-rlvr">Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They move the target to states its own policy rarely visits, expanding reasoning coverage. Prefixes can be wrong; independent verification still defines reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Try continuing an alternative decomposition and check the result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27420-weak-guide-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18d555967dc0fe5d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weak-guide-rlvr" data-paper-title="Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4fb85815b204e8ef">Why mix weak prefixes even though they can be wrong?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweak-guide-rlvr">Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They provide uncommon exploration starts. Entropy truncation limits unstable continuations and native traces maintain coverage. Hints aren&#x27;t labels; use independent verifier. Frozen proxy isn&#x27;t dual-model training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An alternate decomposition can be tried but still receives failure if validation fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27420-weak-guide-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4fb85815b204e8ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weak-guide-rlvr" data-paper-title="Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e84a9eb0b18e84db">How does prefix guidance differ from SFT on complete weak answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweak-guide-rlvr">Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It supplies only a starting point; target generates and learns from reward. Native/guided mixtures and entropy truncation control coverage instead of trusting weak solutions wholesale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give an opening idea without asking the student to copy a wrong conclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27420-weak-guide-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e84a9eb0b18e84db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weak-guide-rlvr" data-paper-title="Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fc7e666f15f6076">Is the local frozen-reference proxy actual dual-checkpoint RLVR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweak-guide-rlvr">Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate distributions simulate guidance. Record mixture proportions and prefix boundaries; keep hints out of independent test. No real two-model generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Numeric alternative starts don&#x27;t measure linguistic weak-prefix quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:video-opsd" data-paper-title="Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-video-opsd-2da91d84" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7da4e86ac722d50">Why does Video-OPSD teacher see evidence frames while student sees full video?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avideo-opsd">Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Privileged frames focus teacher supervision, while student learns to find relevant evidence amid distractions and does not receive annotation at inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher can see the cup pickup moment; student must find it within the full activity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27065-video-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7da4e86ac722d50">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:video-opsd" data-paper-title="Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-14eccc74c245b0fe">Why keep evidence frames teacher-only and full video for student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avideo-opsd">Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Human-labeled frames give focused supervision, weighted by token dependence. Student must handle distractions as deployed; supplying frame labels changes the task. No-video diagnostics aren&#x27;t vision evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>To answer who picked up the cup first, student still needs to locate the relevant segment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27065-video-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-14eccc74c245b0fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:video-opsd" data-paper-title="Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6c24d377aa71a92">How do evidence-dependent weights differ from equal token KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avideo-opsd">Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Emphasize positions influenced by visual evidence, not all style tokens equally. Dependency isn&#x27;t factual certainty. No-video smoke doesn&#x27;t validate paper training time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An action word can depend more on frames than a connective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27065-video-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6c24d377aa71a92">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:video-opsd" data-paper-title="Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-15746459e8aa6d5e">Does local Video-OPSD smoke include video frames?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avideo-opsd">Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Independent reward axes proxy evidence. Available checkpoints don&#x27;t imply trained video model. Align teacher targets to student prefixes and keep annotations out of deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A synthetic process score doesn&#x27;t show the model watched a video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.27065-video-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-15746459e8aa6d5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:uc-mopd" data-paper-title="Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-uc-mopd-4afbd03c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a9ccd364b8ec023">Why expand temperature coverage before UC-MOPD selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Auc-mopd">Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordinary sampling may yield few positive-credit positions. Dual temperatures broaden exploration, then trajectory density/token reliability filter it. More candidates aren&#x27;t all correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Try another solution first, then check whether its steps help.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.26735-uc-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a9ccd364b8ec023">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:uc-mopd" data-paper-title="Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-269cf7e11d08beba">What do temperature expansion, trajectory selection and token gating each solve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Auc-mopd">Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Expand candidate coverage, favor trajectories with dense positive advantages, then gate individual updates with entropy-calibrated probabilities. More samples don&#x27;t guarantee correct supervision; no full teachers locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sample varied solutions, select one with useful steps and reinforce only reliable tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.26735-uc-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-269cf7e11d08beba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:uc-mopd" data-paper-title="Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6280056a50d0c34c">How do positive-advantage density and CLL gating work together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Auc-mopd">Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Density selects useful trajectories; CLL controls local tokens inside selected traces. Both are required and confidence isn&#x27;t truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A generally useful solution can still contain positions not worth reinforcing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.26735-uc-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6280056a50d0c34c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:uc-mopd" data-paper-title="Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-24e5a9dad8d49b28">What does stochastic UC-MOPD gating need to log, and were checkpoints loaded?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Auc-mopd">Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Log probabilities, seed and valid positions so random draws aren&#x27;t deterministic decisions. No general/domain teachers loaded; formula checks don&#x27;t prove retained general capabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Track each differing random mask, not just report the best draw.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.26735-uc-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24e5a9dad8d49b28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clue-opsd" data-paper-title="Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-clue-opsd-7ed80773" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-be66d452b82d5b6e">Why are relevant time intervals privileged training information in Clue-OPSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclue-opsd">Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A focused teacher can guide evidence retrieval in long video. Student still receives full video/question and loses clue and teacher at deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher knows the opening-door timestamp; deployed student must find it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25356">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25356-clue-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be66d452b82d5b6e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clue-opsd" data-paper-title="Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dffc751edf033222">Why query a clue-conditioned teacher on the student&#x27;s own prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclue-opsd">Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actual student prefixes reduce trajectory mismatch while clue segments focus evidence. Clues are training privilege; at inference the student must handle full video without markers, answers or teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Guide correction of an incomplete event ordering during training, without giving the manual clip at deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25356">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25356-clue-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dffc751edf033222">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clue-opsd" data-paper-title="Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8470c0c5f874a93">How does a clue teacher differ from shortening the student&#x27;s video?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclue-opsd">Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shortening input simplifies the task; teacher-only privilege changes supervision while preserving full-video difficulty and costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Seeing a solution clip and seeing all footage are not matched evaluations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25356">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25356-clue-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8470c0c5f874a93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clue-opsd" data-paper-title="Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8caf90bc522fe861">Why score Clue-OPSD KL on student rather than teacher prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclue-opsd">Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Guide actually visited states with aligned token positions despite different visual conditions. The mini-suite does not execute a full video-checkpoint experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the student misidentifies a person, teacher must rate that prefix, not its own ideal opening.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25356">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.25356-clue-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8caf90bc522fe861">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:smopd" data-paper-title="SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-smopd-2a4bef05" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7c3d10ce5b7d86dd">Why specialize then merge in SMOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asmopd">SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Qwen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reward priorities produce complementary teachers. Merge dense supervision on student-visited states instead of forcing conflicting goals into one expert initially. Teachers can still interfere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train rigor and format specialists before deciding how each teaches the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03092-smopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c3d10ce5b7d86dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:smopd" data-paper-title="SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-70fa4e434b261d14">Why train reward-specialized teachers and merge on student states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asmopd">SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Qwen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate rewards produce different strengths, then weighted distillation uses their distributions where students act. This isn&#x27;t averaging rewards into one teacher or merging weights, and abilities can conflict. Local candidate evidence only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Calculation and formatting specialists can both score one student reasoning step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03092-smopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70fa4e434b261d14">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:smopd" data-paper-title="SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-db366732628a378d">How do SMOPD reward specialists differ from MOPD domain specialists?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asmopd">SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Qwen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SMOPD varies reward priorities; MOPD often divides task domains. Both use multiple teachers, but expert grouping/evaluation and budgets differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One domain can have several reward specialists, not one expert per dataset.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03092-smopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db366732628a378d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:smopd" data-paper-title="SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-efc24d49c99b3f4d">Which states should all SMOPD teacher KL terms align to?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asmopd">SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Qwen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Score identical student prefixes, keeping weights/teacher targets frozen. Independent teacher generations do not align positionwise. No real local specialist training/merge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One teacher&#x27;s step two and another&#x27;s step four are not shared supervision states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.03092-smopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efc24d49c99b3f4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rstg" data-paper-title="Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rstg-e8f7dde4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a077cf99039366a7">Why specifically recover all-fail groups in RSTG?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arstg">Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They lack relative reward signal and need teacher correction. All-success also has zero variance but no same failure need; consider variance and reward level.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t call four correct replies a failure group just because their scores tie.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.00782-rstg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a077cf99039366a7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rstg" data-paper-title="Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7b069f4ac14b1cf">Why ask the teacher only for zero-variance failures, not every tied group?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arstg">Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All-fail normalization has no contrast, so teacher examples and high-entropy/gap distillation add signal. Tied successes don&#x27;t need that intervention. Check outcome signs and teacher reliability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Request a verified demonstration for four wrong solutions, not four valid alternatives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.00782-rstg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a7b069f4ac14b1cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rstg" data-paper-title="Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b80daeba0810cc0b">How does RSTG token selection differ from imitating full teacher trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arstg">Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Guide high entropy or large-gap positions more and add SFT on correct teacher traces. Selection avoids some irrelevant signals, but entropy/gap isn&#x27;t ground-truth localization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Focus on uncertain reasoning rather than stable formatting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.00782-rstg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b80daeba0810cc0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rstg" data-paper-title="Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-67bfaf2b24863e43">Does implementing a negative-group gate complete RSTG?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arstg">Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Execute local distillation and teacher-success supervision with provenance/masks. Local candidate objectives do not run large teacher generation or full budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A need_teacher flag does not execute the teacher branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.00782-rstg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67bfaf2b24863e43">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vad" data-paper-title="VAD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-vad-1b365cba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b488d8ea330de209">Why rebuild VAD targets around the current student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avad">VAD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full teacher copying imports style/language bias. Add only visual-direction corrections around student to preserve other preferences; full privileged distribution is weak regularization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Transfer image color evidence without forcing all wording changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b488d8ea330de209">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vad" data-paper-title="VAD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-48b96f2481a2a52d">Why project teacher correction onto visual evidence and keep only aligned components?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avad">VAD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matched views define a visual direction. Keep positive projection and anchor target to student; weakly regularize toward full teacher. This avoids broad stylistic imitation. Local reward axes don&#x27;t reproduce visual training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Try to transfer support for a red object without importing unrelated teacher phrasing preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48b96f2481a2a52d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vad" data-paper-title="VAD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-93258e520a528b62">How does one-sided projection differ from replacing all correction with the visual direction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avad">VAD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep only teacher correction positively aligned to evidence. Replacement ignores whether teacher supported that change. Projection constrains attribution, not correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If teacher correction opposes visual contrast, don&#x27;t blindly inject it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93258e520a528b62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vad" data-paper-title="VAD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-043731ad0bc86318">What should VAD evidence-present and evidence-removed branches share?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Avad">VAD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same frozen teacher, question and student prefix; only evidence view differs. Center logp and stabilize projection. Local process proxy lacks real crops/checkpoint/benchmarks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unrelated text model would confound model architecture with evidence ablation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-043731ad0bc86318">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:crpo" data-paper-title="Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-crpo-a18535ff" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c06cdac5feb0ffce">Why distinguish reflective exploration from exposure bias in CRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acrpo">Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both can be uncertain. Reflection can repair reasoning; exposure bias can compound prefix errors. Group contrast treats them differently instead of rewarding entropy uniformly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rechecking a branch is not the same as drifting after a wrong equation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28026-crpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c06cdac5feb0ffce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:crpo" data-paper-title="Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb12ee1ea24d6bed">Why distinguish reflective and exposure-bias positions rather than reward all high entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acrpo">Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uncertainty can be useful exploration or failure from wrong prefixes. Contrast and privileged self-distillation handle them separately. Entropy alone isn&#x27;t correctness; no complete reasoning training locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>High entropy during a useful recheck and a confused continuation call for different evidence-based updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28026-crpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb12ee1ea24d6bed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:crpo" data-paper-title="Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd450bb59f9c435a">How does CRPO contrast differ from minimizing privileged teacher KL alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acrpo">Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Contrast creates relative competition between positive/negative positions; KL directly matches a target. Classification needs reliability; negatives don&#x27;t eliminate bias automatically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Which negatives appear in the denominator changes the update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28026-crpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd450bb59f9c435a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:crpo" data-paper-title="Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1bf7c072d6c0d5b">Does local CRPO identify real reflection positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acrpo">Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate objectives test masks/diagnostics only. Record position/group provenance, keep privilege out of rollout and never label test positions with gold then claim autonomy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predefined masks don&#x27;t demonstrate finding exposure bias in real text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.28026-crpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1bf7c072d6c0d5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:distilled-rl" data-paper-title="Distilled RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-distilled-rl-b41ef584" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-be4145dd92521d12">How does Distilled RL use teacher distributions inside RL rather than standalone imitation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adistilled-rl">Distilled RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nankai University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher/old-student ratios reweight task advantages at token level for positives only. Task outcome picks reinforcement; teacher focuses credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A verified solution&#x27;s teacher-supported key step can receive extra weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.17247-distilled-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be4145dd92521d12">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:distilled-rl" data-paper-title="Distilled RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-225945cbff9e4ee0">Why add teacher weights only to positive advantages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adistilled-rl">Distilled RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nankai University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verified positive samples already have outcome support; teacher ratio emphasizes useful tokens. Keep nonpositive learning unchanged. Clip and geometric-normalize weights without treating teacher preference as independent truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Boost key steps in success; do not weaken negative updates just for teacher-approved wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.17247-distilled-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-225945cbff9e4ee0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:distilled-rl" data-paper-title="Distilled RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4232f22db291ab10">How does positive-only gating differ from weighting both signs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adistilled-rl">Distilled RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nankai University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nonpositive advantages keep weight one, preserving failure penalties. Two-sided weighting could weaken some negative feedback. The teacher does not relabel outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher preference for wording in a failed reply doesn&#x27;t reduce failure penalty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.17247-distilled-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4232f22db291ab10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:distilled-rl" data-paper-title="Distilled RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c5eea841205341bc">Why normalize clipped ratios by sequence geometric mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adistilled-rl">Distilled RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nankai University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bound ratio scale and make weights relative within a valid-token sequence. Exclude padding and keep nonpositive branch one. Local mini-suite doesn&#x27;t reproduce full generation/training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Including padding changes every weight even if its loss is masked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.17247-distilled-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c5eea841205341bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:armor" data-paper-title="ARMOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-armor-71dc1f8a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d0793b82963f670">Why sample actively from reference in ARMOR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aarmor">ARMOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A passive penalty only acts on visited data and can&#x27;t recover paths current policy never samples. Reference anchors restore actual training coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If student only takes a shortcut, old policy may still generate a verification route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.10481-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d0793b82963f670">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:armor" data-paper-title="ARMOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a68376cc571efdb">How does active reference sampling differ from a KL penalty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aarmor">ARMOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KL constrains drift on sampled states without guaranteeing useful reference behaviors appear. Frozen reference rollouts add that coverage. Anchors may be bad; tune mix and don&#x27;t generalize candidate proxies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Active replay reintroduces the old verification route that a passive penalty may never sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.10481-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a68376cc571efdb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:armor" data-paper-title="ARMOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-85f7219f929ace1d">Are reference rollouts equivalent to adding reference KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aarmor">ARMOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
