<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Rollouts change visited states; KL regularizes distributions on existing states. Anchors may be stale or wrong and need evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A missing old solution isn&#x27;t practiced merely because KL is present.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.10481-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-85f7219f929ace1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:armor" data-paper-title="ARMOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a88eac1ccf377ad">What is local ARMOR reference, and are its samples on-policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aarmor">ARMOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The initialized candidate policy; log anchors separately from current student samples. No paper long-horizon pool; mixing tests data flow, not stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t label an old-policy action as generated by the current policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2607.10481-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a88eac1ccf377ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mopd" data-paper-title="MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mopd-f0fd48c7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d026bf7949d24011">Why train independent domain teachers first in MOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amopd">MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaomi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint RL can couple domain gradients. Separate specialists optimize their domains before sharing dense student-prefix supervision. Integration still shares parameters and can interfere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train math and code teachers separately, then guide one student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d026bf7949d24011">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mopd" data-paper-title="MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2bf256351a9b963">Why query multiple teachers on student traces rather than concatenate expert traces?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amopd">MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaomi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actual student prefixes reveal visited states. Matched teachers give dense supervision there, reducing trajectory mismatch. Supervision fusion isn&#x27;t parameter averaging or guaranteed skill retention; local evidence is candidate-level.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both teachers can guide a mixed math/code intermediate state absent from their complete answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2bf256351a9b963">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mopd" data-paper-title="MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-92e43d22fe015b99">Where do probability mixture and parameter averaging merge teachers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amopd">MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaomi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probability mixtures form supervision at shared student states and require teacher inference. Parameter averaging directly combines comparable weights and can disrupt coordination. No superiority without matched experiments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding output distributions differs from averaging weight matrices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92e43d22fe015b99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mopd" data-paper-title="MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-448c87336997f6e1">What must MOPD teacher weights and dimensions satisfy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amopd">MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaomi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Align vocabulary/candidates and normalize weights by the defined rule. Freeze teachers and update student only. Deterministic mini-suite teachers aren&#x27;t trained specialists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different vocabulary IDs don&#x27;t align merely by renormalizing the sum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-448c87336997f6e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:polaris-hri" data-paper-title="POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-polaris-hri-c07af119" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a8b284fd70c36138">Why add a teacher-forced reference story to POLARIS policy stories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apolaris-hri">POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long story evaluation is sparse; a reference anchors quality under the same external rubric. It is additional training supervision, not test gold or a supplied copyrighted story.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Practice with a reference story but generate independently at evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04095v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.04095-polaris-hri/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a8b284fd70c36138">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:polaris-hri" data-paper-title="POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-502cc3028b75390d">Why use policy-only statistics and gradually add reference advantage in POLARIS HRI?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apolaris-hri">POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Including reference in mean/SD would change every policy advantage. Use policy-only stats, scale reference gradually from zero, and apply identical rubric. Local component isn&#x27;t full long-story training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five policy stories determine baseline; reference computes its own advantage against them, not inside their average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04095v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.04095-polaris-hri/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-502cc3028b75390d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:polaris-hri" data-paper-title="POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-edb4c07a49fae20e">How does gradual reference injection differ from equal mixing at the start?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apolaris-hri">POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference weight rises from zero to avoid early domination; policy stories alone determine mean/variance. Equal mixing changes strength and potentially baselines.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reference advantage weight at step zero must be zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04095v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.04095-polaris-hri/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-edb4c07a49fae20e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:polaris-hri" data-paper-title="POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-117cbaa22780a1d9">How does POLARIS avoid overflow without changing clipped objective?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apolaris-hri">POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choose the exact branch by advantage sign in log-ratio space, clear padding/zero advantage first and exponentiate afterward. No extra clamp. Full story training was too costly; tensor gradients aren&#x27;t capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A capped branch doesn&#x27;t need to compute a huge exp before taking min.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04095v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.04095-polaris-hri/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-117cbaa22780a1d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcd" data-paper-title="OPCD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opcd-d21234a6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-198f7d6d31dcfc23">What context-dependent learning can OPCD preserve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcd">OPCD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prompt, retrieval or past experience vanishes when context clears. Distill a context-rich teacher into a context-free student on its own trajectories to internalize behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn a tool-use lesson that remains useful when the hint is absent next time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12275">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.12275-opcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-198f7d6d31dcfc23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcd" data-paper-title="OPCD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0cb6a3f7ec32a4d">Why roll out without experience and score with an experience-aware teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcd">OPCD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Internalize external knowledge rather than preserve dependency. Student gets task only; teacher scores same prefix with experience; update by student-to-teacher reverse KL. Reliability matters and local checks don&#x27;t reproduce long system prompts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Remove the instruction at evaluation to test whether the operation lesson lives in weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12275">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.12275-opcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0cb6a3f7ec32a4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcd" data-paper-title="OPCD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad9048a85aaafb61">How does OPCD differ from retrieving the same experience at inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcd">OPCD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval depends on external context and read cost. Distillation reduces that dependence but can forget or overgeneralize. They can complement each other; compare empirically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updated documents can be swapped immediately; older knowledge distilled into weights doesn&#x27;t automatically update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12275">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.12275-opcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad9048a85aaafb61">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcd" data-paper-title="OPCD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cacfa0f1be011404">What is OPCD reverse-KL direction and student input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcd">OPCD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KL from no-experience student to experience-conditioned teacher on identical student prefix. Experience stays teacher-only. Local conditional distributions aren&#x27;t long prompts or paper environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapping numerator to teacher changes KL direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12275">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.12275-opcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cacfa0f1be011404">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opsd" data-paper-title="OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opsd-096ec0f1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8dc4d92c145bd08">Why can the same model be a more informed OPSD teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopsd">OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Los Angeles</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher additionally sees a verified solution, while student gets problem only. The difference is information, not model size. It depends on reliable solutions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Judging with the conclusion known differs from solving it independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8dc4d92c145bd08">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opsd" data-paper-title="OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-33c5b265f43889b1">Why must OPSD student rollouts not see the verified solution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopsd">OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Los Angeles</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher uses it to score actual student prefixes; student stays in deployment conditions. Pointwise clipping bounds stylistic outliers. Giving student the answer bypasses learning. Local checks cover mechanism only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher can evaluate a half-completed derivation knowing the answer; student cannot use that answer during independent generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-33c5b265f43889b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opsd" data-paper-title="OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fe169a95f58fd9d">How does OPSD isolation differ from answer-conditioned SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopsd">OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Los Angeles</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hide solution during student sampling and score its states with privileged teacher. Adding solution to student would teach unavailable deployment dependence. Full distribution distillation isn&#x27;t imitation of one answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A useful intermediate expression can appear for teacher but not as a shortcut in student prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fe169a95f58fd9d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opsd" data-paper-title="OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c3aec8cf1f24e30">Why clip OPSD pointwise rather than one response coefficient?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopsd">OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Los Angeles</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Limit per-token divergence so unusual stylistic positions cannot dominate. Freeze teacher target and align masks. Local views aren&#x27;t Qwen competition-math training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One anomalous format token needn&#x27;t amplify the entire sequence&#x27;s guidance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c3aec8cf1f24e30">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ragcompass" data-paper-title="RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ragcompass-a7b92c9e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-236494f1a7102ca0">Why does RAGCompass score an evidence bundle instead of predicting a retriever&#x27;s name?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aragcompass">RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-06 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One shared reranker reads each retriever&#x27;s evidence bundle; candidates are not tied to fixed IDs. A new retriever can be scored if it returns the same kind of evidence, but that interface property alone guarantees no transfer gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Five passages from a new vector retriever can compete with five from an existing BM25 retriever. A binary head trained on BM25 and an older vector retriever has no class for the new one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 论文离线与线上效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05596v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.05596-ragcompass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-236494f1a7102ca0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ragcompass" data-paper-title="RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d8ba1f51584631d9">Why does RAGCompass compute KL along the candidate axis of one query?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aragcompass">RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-06 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each utility is the fixed reader&#x27;s answer F1 for one evidence bundle. Softmax turns utilities for the same query into a training target. For KL(target || prediction), the score gradient is p − u. Normalizing across queries would change the objective of choosing evidence separately for each request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: With p = (0.5, 0.5) and u = (0.8, 0.2), the gradient is (−0.3, 0.3), so gradient descent raises the first candidate&#x27;s relative score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05596v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.05596-ragcompass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d8ba1f51584631d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ragcompass" data-paper-title="RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f30740ae3afcdd60">How does answer-utility supervision differ from passage relevance supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aragcompass">RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-06 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An individually relevant passage need not make the complete evidence set sufficient. RAGCompass supervises routing with answer F1 from a fixed reader using the whole bundle. This reflects complementary evidence and reader behavior, but it also ties the target to the chosen reader and reference labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One bundle supplies a relevant biography passage; another also supplies the event date. When the question asks when the event happened, the second bundle is more likely to yield high answer F1.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 论文离线与线上效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05596v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.05596-ragcompass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f30740ae3afcdd60">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ragcompass" data-paper-title="RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfff2f4eb43da12f">Why does the 0.05 utility-gap filter stay out of inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aragcompass">RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-06 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The utility gap requires reference answers to compute F1 and is therefore an offline filter, not a routing feature. Inference receives candidate scores only and selects the largest. Objective and gradient tests, a label-free API, and real distribution-shift evaluations are distinct evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Offline training can discard candidates with F1 0.52 and 0.50 because their gap is 0.02. A live request has no gold answer and must still choose using the actual model scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05596v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.05596-ragcompass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfff2f4eb43da12f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:bopd" data-paper-title="Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-bopd-82866624" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f665514d3bf7ec10">Why not continue training the Stage I student during BOPD Stage II?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abopd">Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>BOPD separates teacher construction from transfer. The Stage I student becomes the frozen intermediate teacher. Stage II restores the student exactly to M0 and creates a fresh optimizer. Retaining Stage I student parameters or momentum changes the method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For example, a weight moving from 1 to 1.2 in Stage I remains 1.2 in the teacher, while the fresh student returns to 1; both must not start at 1.2.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13680v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.13680-bopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f665514d3bf7ec10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:bopd" data-paper-title="Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8dcb5300d4c05f30">Should BOPD FKL average every token in the batch together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abopd">Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Average valid tokens within each student trajectory, then average trajectories. Preserve teacher-to-student KL and detach teacher distributions. A flat token average gives longer responses more weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For response lengths 1 and 3 with losses 2 and all zeros respectively, equal-trajectory loss is 1, whereas a flat token average is .5.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13680v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.13680-bopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8dcb5300d4c05f30">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:bopd" data-paper-title="Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-de5f2c73ae2a0bcb">How does BOPD&#x27;s teacher context differ from continued reference-conditioned OPSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abopd">Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stage I uses the reference-conditioned frozen initial teacher to construct an intermediate. Stage II freezes that intermediate and removes references, so teacher and student share observable context. Renaming a teacher or giving the student the reference is not equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The Stage I teacher sees the problem and verified solution. In Stage II both models see only the problem and fresh-student prefix; reference-conditioned scores cannot be reused as though they were reference-free.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:bopd" data-paper-title="Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3c7620c9b2b9983f">Do the handoff and CUDA checks establish a complete BOPD reproduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abopd">Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local execution covers actual FKL, module copies, buffer restoration, a frozen teacher and a fresh optimizer. LLM rollouts, reference prompts and full two-stage training are absent. The mathematical FKL also does not implement the unaudited Appendix pointwise clipping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A zero restoration error in a small Linear module checks handoff only. The source additionally uses 2-4 GPUs, 3,200 student rollouts per stage and up to 38,912-token evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与代码映射, 结果、负控与边界, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lcs-reference-opd" data-paper-title="Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-lcs-reference-opd-4da7031c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-41b7715738107eb6">Why not choose any similar successful trajectory for a failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alcs-reference-opd">Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · Georgia Institute of Technology（工作在Amazon Web Services实习期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success validates its own task, not compatibility with the failed path. Select from reward-validated successes of the same task instance using ordered executed-action LCS. Even an identical cross-task sequence cannot bypass that boundary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two room tasks may both contain a take-cup action but start with different cabinets and inventory. The other task&#x27;s actions are not automatically a valid reference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13135v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.13135-lcs-reference-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-41b7715738107eb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lcs-reference-opd" data-paper-title="Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ed55cbdd21618b1f">Can the ALFWorld and tau3 normalizers be silently unified?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alcs-reference-opd">Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · Georgia Institute of Technology（工作在Amazon Web Services实习期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. ALFWorld divides by the shorter trajectory length, while tau3 divides by the failed length. The former measures agreement relative to the shorter sequence; the latter measures failed-sequence coverage. Rankings can reverse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For failure length 6, a length 2 reference matching 2 scores 1 under shorter normalization; a length 5 reference matching 4 scores .8. Failed normalization instead gives 1/3 and 2/3 and selects the longer reference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13135v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.13135-lcs-reference-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ed55cbdd21618b1f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lcs-reference-opd" data-paper-title="Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c06f477f4adc499d">Do more LCS matches prove that actions occur in identical states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alcs-reference-opd">Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · Georgia Institute of Technology（工作在Amazon Web Services实习期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Prefix matching has a state interpretation under shared initial conditions and deterministic transitions. After skipping unmatched actions, LCS additionally requires recoverable detours. Irreversible database writes or object moves can change later action meaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An extra look may preserve the state and rejoin a route. An extra delete-record changes the database, so a later identical query need not see the same state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 论文离线与线上效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13135v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.13135-lcs-reference-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c06f477f4adc499d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lcs-reference-opd" data-paper-title="Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b382e90888a4b72b">Why neither one-to-one reference matching nor a full-batch loss denominator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alcs-reference-opd">Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · Georgia Institute of Technology（工作在Amazon Web Services实习期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Free-target OT does not constrain reference frequencies, so multiple failures may choose the same best reference independently. Only failures are updated and the loss divides by their count. All-success batches skip the optimizer rather than applying momentum or decay with zero loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two failures may both choose reference A. If only 2 of 3 rollouts fail with losses 2 and 6, their mean is 4, not 8/3.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13135v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2611.13135-lcs-reference-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b382e90888a4b72b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

How can a teacher with answers, visual evidence, or specialist hints help a student that cannot see them?

## Takeaway

Teacher and student may be different conditional views of one model. OPSD gives the training teacher verified answers or reasoning while the student sees only deployable inputs. Multiple teachers and token routing select who supervises each position. Check how the extra information changes supervision, whether it suits the student, and whether it erodes already successful behavior.

## Example

A student misreads a chart scale. A training teacher sees a crop or explanation and can give a correction distribution on the same student prefix. The student is updated with nonprivileged inputs. If math and code use separate experts, soft routing combines valid probabilities in a common vocabulary; averaging logits is not the same as mixing predictive distributions.

## Common pitfall

Privileged references stay inside allowed training-teacher or scorer boundaries, not evaluated student inputs. A more confident teacher may be wrong; multiple teachers may not complement each other. Two-view, routing, and gradient components are not complete model distillation. Keep high-cost non-reproduction and local diagnostic boundaries visible.

## Reading order

Read OPSD for shared parameters with different conditioning, Token-Level Teacher Selection for positionwise routing and mixtures, and MOPD for capability conflict and retention across teachers.

1. [OPSD](../../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18734)
2. [Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21234v1)
3. [MOPD](../../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30406)

## Check your understanding

If the same model acts as teacher and student, is there necessarily no new signal?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    No. Identical parameters can yield different conditional distributions under different evidence, contexts, or reasoning paths. That difference can train the student, but its benefit must be tested. Identical distributions or irrelevant style differences do not promise stable gains.

</details>
